title: The Quarter-End Illusion: The GST Sitting in Your Account Isn't Actually Yours
linkedin:
The September quarter just closed. If your bank balance looks healthier than usual, a chunk of it probably isn't yours yet.

Every invoice raised over the last three months carried a GST component, collected on behalf of the tax office. Unless it's been actively separated out, it sits in the same account as trading profit and everything else, right up until the October BAS deadline turns it into an outgoing.

None of this is a compliance gap. Your bookkeeper or BAS agent will record and lodge it accurately regardless. The gap sits one layer up, in whether spending decisions this quarter were made against the full balance or the smaller, genuinely free one.

The pattern repeats every quarter for the same reason. Cash builds, it feels like room to move, and the BAS deadline lands in the same fortnight as the superannuation guarantee payment for the same period. Nothing about either bill is a surprise on its own. The timing collision is what catches businesses out.

The fix isn't a bigger finance function. It's treating GST the way most businesses already treat super, money that belongs to someone else the moment it's collected, moved into its own place before it gets counted as spendable.
